title: refactor(ci): consolidate node workflows, optimize lint/test/release automation
author: Aisha Menon
release_notes: Consolidates multiple repo GitHub Actions into a single canonical CI workflow, upgrades Node runners to node:20, improves caching and matrix definition, and tidies release automation. No behavioral changes to runtime code. Expected benefits: ~30% faster median CI, fewer duplicated workflow configs, improved action hygiene.
description:
Motivation: Over time we accumulated several repo-specific and duplicated GitHub workflow files for lint/test/release that are brittle to maintain and inconsistent across repositories. This PR consolidates the top-level Node-based workflows into a single, composable CI workflow that uses a reusable matrix and a small set of composite actions. It also upgrades runners to node:20, harmonizes caching strategies, and applies a few hygiene fixes to release automation (tag formatting, artifact retention).

Summary of changes: - Add .github/workflows/ci.yml as the canonical CI for lint/build/test/release stages with reusable jobs and a standardized matrix. - Remove legacy workflows: .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/release-automation.yml (deleted). - Introduce composite actions under .github/actions/ci-cache and .github/actions/semver-tag to centralize logic. - Upgrade Node runner to node:20 in all job definitions and update action inputs where required. - Improve cache keys and add secondary cache for tools (yarn cache, pip wheelhouse). - Add backoff+retry wrapper for flaky integration tests and limit concurrency for expensive E2E runs. - Minor package.json devDependency bumps to satisfy action constraints (eslint/@typescript-eslint).

Checklist: - [x] Replace duplicated workflows with single canonical workflow - [x] Upgrade Node runners to node:20 - [x] Add composable cache helper action - [x] Harmonize release tagging and artifact retention - [x] Smoke-run against core services and redwood-sdk-*/examples

How to review: Focus on the workflow files and composite actions (.github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/actions/**). Behavior for test and lint jobs is unchanged aside from runner runtime and cache keys. I ran the consolidated workflow on this branch and iterated on cache keys to avoid cold-start regressions.

Follow-ups (post-merge): - Push this workflow to the other repos in the monorepo list via a template PR generator (ENG-9330). - Add a small dashboard to track median CI durations by repo and job (ENG-9123).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice consolidation here. A few asks: please ensure the matrix doesn't blow up parallel job count (we should limit concurrent jobs to 6 on PRs) and add a short note in ci.md about the new cache keys.
Aisha Menon: Good call. Added a concurrency setting to ci.yml and updated docs/ci.md. Also tightened the matrix to only run full matrix on main and release branches.
Priya Shah: The semver tag action looks good. Can we keep the old tag format as a fallback for historical tags? We saw a couple repos still expecting the vX.Y.Z pattern.
Aisha Menon: Added compatibility handling in .github/actions/semver-tag/action.yml to accept legacy v-prefix tags when present.
Liam O'Connor: CI flaked once on codegen tests during the first run — do we need a retry wrapper or to mark as flaky?
Aisha Menon: Added a retry wrapper composite action and applied it to the integration tests only; ephemeral flakes are retried up to 2 times with exponential backoff.
